subject: Starlit AI onboarding — throughput & resilience certification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anika Shah <anika@starlit.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Starlit AI — onboarding benchmark plan and initial cadence

Hi Anika, Monica, Karthik, Vivek —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Starlit's production launch timeline looks like late July, so our goal for this onboarding sprint is to validate throughput and latency targets and give you an actionable remediation plan before your pilot cutover.

Quick bullets / ask:
- Can Starlit confirm the target traffic shape (concurrent users and percent of long vs short prompts)?
- Proposed test window: next week (June 2–4) for smoke + ramp, then a validation run June 6. Doable?
- We’ll run two model variants: redwood/decoder-large (baseline) and redwood/decoder-large-quant (cost-optimized).

Internal owners: Monica will lead coordination and evidence collection; Karthik will run the load tests and analyze traces; Vivek will advise on batching/quantization knobs if we hit unit-cost regressions.

Attaching a short run plan (v1) — will refine after Anika confirms traffic.

Next steps: Anika — confirm traffic shape and a preferred test window. Monica — I’ll hand to you to own the schedule once Anika confirms.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: starlit_onboard_runplan_v1.csv]

From: Anika Shah <anika@starlit.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starlit AI — onboarding benchmark plan and initial cadence

Thanks Ben —

We can do the June 2–6 window. Quick details from our side:
- Production target: 120–150 sustained inference req/s for the recommendation endpoint (avg payload ~420 tokens).
- Peak concurrent sessions expected: ~180 (short chats + batched recommendation calls).
- SLA goal: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for typical prompts (<= 500 tokens); tail latency (p99) target <= 800ms.
- We’ll provide an anonymized sample corpus and a staging API key (staging@starlit) by EOD May 31.

Notes: We ran an internal spike last month and saw p99 spikes during model cold starts and concurrent cache misses. We’d like Redwood to include warmup and cache-priming guidance in the runbook.

Anika Shah
Head of Infrastructure, Starlit AI
Anika Shah | Starlit AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@starlit.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starlit AI — onboarding benchmark plan and initial cadence

Thanks Anika — good context. A few technical clarifications before we finalize the run plan:

1) Exact request distribution — can you confirm proportion: (a) short recommendation calls (~80 tokens) vs (b) mid-context queries (~420 tokens) vs (c) long-form persona prompts (~1,200 tokens)? We need this to pick batching and KV-cache parameters.
2) Sequence length limit for the two endpoints — are you enforcing 2k or 4k tokens?
3) Will the staging key allow us to run up to 200 rps for 30 minutes? If not, we’ll need an elevated temporary test key.
4) Can you provide the anonymized sample traces (timestamps + payload sizes) so our load generator can replay realistic inter-arrival times?

Planned acceptance checks we’ll run (short summary):
- Steady-state throughput at 150 rps for 15m with avg token length 420 — measure p50/p95/p99 and error rate
- Concurrency ramp: step from 20 -> 180 sessions over 30 minutes to observe tail latency behavior
- Cold-start exercise: deploy a model variant and throttle traffic to observe cold-start latencies and cache warmup curve

I’ve attached a draft CSV with the proposed traffic mix. If you can confirm the distribution and token limits we’ll lock the detailed schedule and runbook.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: starlit_onboard_runplan_v1.csv]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@starlit.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starlit AI — onboarding benchmark plan and initial cadence

Hi all —

Thanks for the confirmations and technical notes. Attached is the Redwood runbook (redwood_runbook_v2.pdf) — it includes the exact commands we’ll execute, the thresholds we’ll check, and a short checklist for evidence collection. Key acceptance criteria summarized here for quick reference:

Acceptance criteria (pass / fail buckets):
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for avg 420-token requests on redwood/decoder-large (baseline). p99 should be < 800ms except during cold-start windows.
- Throughput: sustain 150 req/s for 15 continuous minutes with error rate < 0.5% on the baseline.
- Resilience: after a simulated node loss (we’ll schedule one induced failure), the request success rate should remain >= 98% and 95th latency degradation should be <= 1.5x baseline.
- Cost fallback: if baseline can’t meet throughput without violating p95 targets, we’ll attempt the quantized variant and measure unit-cost delta.

Run cadence (high level):
- Smoke + warmup (June 2): 60 min low traffic, cache priming, validation of telemetry hooks
- Ramp tests (June 3): step ramp to peak with telemetry capture
- Validation run (June 6, 09:00–10:00 PT): 15m steady-state at 150rps + node-failure window

\Artifacts we’ll collect and share: run logs, tprof traces, token-level cost report, and a CSV with p50/p95/p99 over time.

Links: run artifacts and the HubSpot deal are attached to the HubSpot record (link below). Please upload any customer-side traces to the Drive folder so we can co-locate evidence.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aStarlitOnboardDrive
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/9073/deal/DEAL-9073-STL

Attachments included: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf, starlit_onboard_runplan_v1.csv

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Customer Success
[Attachment: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf]

From: Anika Shah <anika@starlit.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Starlit AI — onboarding benchmark plan and initial cadence

Monica / team —

Quick update from the validation run this morning (we ran the steady-state window and the induced node fault):
- Steady-state (150rps, avg 420 tokens): p95 = 285ms, p99 = 760ms, errors = 0.3% — PASS against p95 and error targets.
- After induced node loss: success rate dropped to 97.6% briefly (inside the 5-min window), p95 rose to ~430ms for two intervals; p99 climbed to 1.2s. We captured traces and stack logs.
- Cold-starts still produce p99 spikes > 1.4s for a small percentage when KV cache misses occur.

We’re attaching our CSV with per-minute aggregates and a short note on reproduction steps for the node-failure window. Overall, we’re comfortable moving forward with the pilot but would like Redwood’s recommendation on mitigations for the tail latency (warmup priming, pre-warming pools, or conservative autoscale thresholds).

Sharing artifacts:
[Attachment: initial-kpi-snapshot-20270606.csv]
Drive: I uploaded traces to the shared folder above.

Anika Shah
Head of Infrastructure, Starlit AI
